edges.notes: Container images unpack into a runtime bundle (rootfs + config.json) governed by the runtime spec.
Linux namespaces, cgroups, and capabilities are the dominant backing primitives described in the spec.
runc is the OCI reference implementation for executing bundles per the runtime spec.
crun is an alternative OCI runtime implementation on Linux conforming to the same spec.
Engine stack ultimately executes OCI bundles via a low-level runtime (commonly runc-class) implementing this spec.
Creates and supervises OCI bundles; invokes low-level runtimes conforming to the runtime spec.
kubelet/CRI path runs containers as OCI bundles on Linux nodes in typical stacks.
Podman generates and runs OCI bundles using a configurable low-level runtime implementing the spec.
CRI-O runs pods via OCI bundles and a low-level OCI runtime implementing the spec.
Runtime bundles specify rootfs; Linux toolchains may assemble that rootfs using overlay mounts — orthogonal to the runtime spec text.
Kata Containers provides an OCI-compatible runtime implementation that executes bundles with VM-level isolation on supported Linux stacks.
gVisor’s runsc is an OCI-compatible runtime implementation that executes bundles with userspace syscall interposition on supported Linux stacks.
